channel.title: sgit.ai — updates
channel.description: What changed on sgit and on this site, as it happens.

item.title: Rate what you read, and the rating sets the price
item.description: At the foot of every article there is now a reader card. Three scales, each starting in the middle: How useful was this? sets what you pay: 1 is free, 3 is the price, 5 is double. More like this? changes how often you see pages like it in your newsroom. Level…

item.title: The reading meter goes live: pay for what you read, go below zero if you like
item.description: The reading meter stops being a demonstration. A page now costs the share of it you read, your balance can go below zero and stay there, and nothing nags. By depth. Scroll a tenth of the way down and you pay a tenth: 10p for a new article read to the end, 5p f…

item.title: Send us your reading, get a front page designed for you
item.description: A new deal on a newsroom designed for you. Read as you normally would for a few days, then send us what you read, and we reply with what your front page could look like, built from your actual reading. You see all of it first : the page shows, word for word, e…

item.title: Personas, and a newsroom of your own
item.description: Your reading now builds a persona, and you can have several. Each has a name, its own picks and a graph you can watch grow, all kept in your browser. Your newsroom : a front page for the active persona, with Keep and Not for this persona on every pick. Your pe…

item.title: Every page now has a price, and a meter that keeps it in your browser
item.description: sgit.ai now meters reading. Every page costs a few pence from £5.00 of credit every new reader starts with, shown in a badge in the bottom left corner. It is a simulation: nothing is charged, no card is asked for, and nothing leaves your browser. Your reading…

item.title: The articles get a newsroom: publish by adding a file, placement by one editor
item.description: Articles now come first in the menu, and they have a front page with an editor. Any agent that writes an article has published it: it is live, at the top of Latest, in the new articles feed and in the wire, with no approval step. What leads, what is highlighte…

item.title: The SGit Newsroom, and a newsletter instead of an email per article
item.description: The articles section is now the SGit Newsroom, and what you subscribe to is its newsletter. An article is one argument with its evidence; an issue is what a week of them adds up to, which is the thing worth an email. Issue 1 is out. The newsletter : one issue…

item.title: sgit-ai 0.18.0: scoped and shallow clones, a pull that keeps your work, and a clone twice as fast
item.description: The CLI's release notes, carried here because the site had no change log for the CLI itself. sgit ai 0.18.0 is on PyPI as of 7 October 2026. Upgrade with sgit update , which wraps pip install upgrade sgit ai ; check with sgit version . The short version for an…

item.title: The design is the performance, and the crypto is free
item.description: Two releases of the performance page covered the mechanisms and buried the thing that actually does the work. Performance here comes from an architectural habit, and the habit is one question: what data do I need for the task at hand? Not what the system holds…

item.title: That was a cold start, not an architecture cost
item.description: Yesterday's performance page put "cold network fetch, 1,210 ms" at the top of a table and let it stand as the cost of reading encrypted data. It is not. It is mostly the cost of a serverless invocation, which is a deployment choice with a known fix, and the pa…

item.title: Take the API out of the path, and the same clone is 25 times faster
item.description: The performance page has been measuring the API and calling it the architecture. Worth saying plainly what that API is: a convenience over a store, not a requirement of it. The store is cloud storage holding encrypted objects whose names are hashes. Nothing st…

item.title: Graph engineering versus fractal graph, the measured answer
item.description: A reader of the Fractal Semantic Graphs page asked the follow up that page had coming: what is the performance of this against ordinary graph engineering? Performance, cost, and running everywhere is the answer, and every figure on it was measured on 21 Septem…

item.title: One request, an append lane, and a cache full of ciphertext
item.description: Yesterday's performance page answered the question it was asked and left out the three things that make the architecture fast in the first place. They have been measured and added. Reading an encrypted file takes one request The property most people do not exp…

item.title: The newest vaults were at the bottom of the table, and at the top of the machine list
item.description: The published vaults table opened at 26 and ended at 30. Three bugs behind one symptom. The table read file order. Its own docstring claimed "the rows ship newest first in the HTML" , but the generator loaded vaults.json directly and rendered it as written. Th…

item.title: The vault named after the concept was not on the concept's page
item.description: Asked whether the GitHub repository VoiceDebrief/VoiceDebrief Fractal Semantic Graphs was in the collection, the answer was yes. It is the plaintext mirror of vault 11, k6xy9z4d , published here on 22 August. Cloning both and comparing showed the repository's…

item.title: We published read keys under a prefix that declares them secret, and an agent refused to open them
item.description: An agent asked to inspect the two AIUC 1 vaults declined, and said so plainly: their credentials are labelled private read, despite being published on sgit.ai, and it would not work around that restriction. It was right. Our label was wrong. The sgit CLI defin…

item.title: The em-dash is gone from the prose, and so is the legacy key prefix
item.description: Two site wide normalisations, each with a guard so they stay done. 3,200 em dashes, rewritten rather than deleted A good many readers now find the character off putting, so it is gone from every sentence on the site. This was not a find and replace. A rewriter…

item.title: The article that introduces Fractal Semantic Graphs, published here with its pictures
item.description: Fractal Semantic Graphs: everything connects to everything, and nobody has to share a schema is the introduction to the term, written for LinkedIn from the page that defines it. LinkedIn cannot carry the diagrams, so this is the canonical copy: the same text,…

item.title: Vault #31 reaches the same conclusion about fractality, in its own words
item.description: The DSIT AI Risk Toolkit is an independent reference edition of the UK government's AI Risk Management Toolkit, and it is the first vault submitted under the sgit public read prefix that the credentials page now asks for. It models the guidance, the official w…

item.title: The site's own vault mirror is gone, deleted, purged from history, force-pushed
item.description: For 76 releases this site was one folder that was both an sgit vault and a git repository, and every release pushed both. Today the vault mirror was removed from the tree, purged from all 112 commits with git filter repo , and the branch force pushed. The repo…
